solution:
Combine the four terms with \(\log m - \log n = \log\frac{m}{n}\) and \(\log m + \log n = \log(mn)\):
\(= \log_{10}\left(\frac{28}{45}\times\frac{324}{35}\times\frac{325}{432}\times\frac{15}{13}\right)\).
Cancel step by step: \(\frac{28}{45}\times\frac{324}{35} = \frac{144}{25}\), then \(\frac{144}{25}\times\frac{325}{432} = \frac{13}{3}\), then \(\frac{13}{3}\times\frac{15}{13} = 5\).
\(\therefore\) the expression \(= \log_{10} 5\).

Write the right side as a single logarithm:
\(\frac{1}{2}(\log a + \log b) = \frac{1}{2}\log(ab) = \log\sqrt{ab}\).
So \(\log\left(\frac{a+b}{2}\right) = \log\sqrt{ab}\), and since \(\log\) is one-one, \(\frac{a+b}{2} = \sqrt{ab}\).
Hence \(a + b = 2\sqrt{ab}\), i.e. \(a - 2\sqrt{ab} + b = 0\), i.e. \(\left(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}\right)^2 = 0\).
\(\therefore \sqrt{a} = \sqrt{b}\), and squaring, \(a = b\).

Take logarithms of both sides of \(b^2 = ac\) (both sides are positive):
\(\log b^2 = \log(ac)\).
Using \(\log m^n = n\log m\) on the left and \(\log(mn) = \log m + \log n\) on the right,
\(2\log b = \log a + \log c\).
\(\therefore \log a + \log c = 2\log b\).

Combine the left side: \(\log_x(8x-3) - \log_x 4 = \log_x\left(\frac{8x-3}{4}\right)\).
So \(\log_x\left(\frac{8x-3}{4}\right) = 2\), which means \(\frac{8x-3}{4} = x^2\).
Hence \(4x^2 - 8x + 3 = 0\), i.e. \((2x-1)(2x-3) = 0\), giving \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) or \(x = \frac{3}{2}\).
Both values are admissible bases: each is positive and not equal to \(1\); also \(8x-3\) is positive for each, being \(1\) when \(x=\frac{1}{2}\) and \(9\) when \(x=\frac{3}{2}\).
\(\therefore x = \frac{3}{2}\) or \(x = \frac{1}{2}\).

Add \(2ab\) to the given relation: \(a^2 + b^2 + 2ab = 7ab + 2ab\), so \((a+b)^2 = 9ab\).
Divide by \(9\): \(\left(\frac{a+b}{3}\right)^2 = ab\).
Take logarithms: \(2\log\left(\frac{a+b}{3}\right) = \log(ab) = \log a + \log b\).
\(\therefore \log\left(\frac{a+b}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\log a + \frac{1}{2}\log b\).

The right side is \(\frac{1}{2}\log x + \frac{1}{2}\log y = \frac{1}{2}\log(xy) = \log\sqrt{xy}\).
So \(\log\left(\frac{x-y}{5}\right) = \log\sqrt{xy}\), giving \(\frac{x-y}{5} = \sqrt{xy}\), i.e. \(x - y = 5\sqrt{xy}\).
Squaring both sides: \(x^2 - 2xy + y^2 = 25xy\).
\(\therefore x^2 + y^2 = 27xy\).

Peel the logarithms one at a time, using \(\log_b N = m \Rightarrow N = b^m\).
\(\log_3\left[\log_2(\log_3 x)\right] = 1 \Rightarrow \log_2(\log_3 x) = 3^1 = 3\).
\(\log_2(\log_3 x) = 3 \Rightarrow \log_3 x = 2^3 = 8\).
\(\log_3 x = 8 \Rightarrow x = 3^8\).
\(\therefore x = 6561\).

Here \(f(t) = \log(1-t)\), so substitute into each side.
Left side: \(f\left(\frac{1}{1+x}\right) = \log\left(1 - \frac{1}{1+x}\right) = \log\left(\frac{x}{1+x}\right) = \log x - \log(1+x)\).
Right side: \(f(1-x) = \log\left(1-(1-x)\right) = \log x\) and \(f(-x) = \log\left(1-(-x)\right) = \log(1+x)\),
so \(f(1-x) - f(-x) = \log x - \log(1+x)\).
Both sides are \(\log x - \log(1+x)\).
\(\therefore f\left(\frac{1}{1+x}\right) = f(1-x) - f(-x)\).

Prove each inequality by clearing the logarithm with a suitable power.
Left inequality: \(\log_{10}3 > \frac{2}{5} \iff 3 > 10^{2/5} \iff 3^5 > 10^2\) (raising both sides to the 5th power), and \(243 > 100\) is true.
Right inequality: \(\log_{10}3 < \frac{1}{2} \iff 3 < 10^{1/2} \iff 3^2 < 10\) (squaring), and \(9 < 10\) is true.
\(\therefore \frac{2}{5} < \log_{10}3 < \frac{1}{2}\).

Using \(n\log m = \log m^n\) and \(\log m + \log n = \log(mn)\), the left side equals
\(\log\left[\left(\frac{15}{16}\right)^7\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)^6\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^5\left(\frac{32}{25}\right)\right]\).
Write each base in primes: \(\frac{15}{16} = \frac{3\cdot 5}{2^4},\ \frac{8}{3} = \frac{2^3}{3},\ \frac{2}{5},\ \frac{32}{25} = \frac{2^5}{5^2}\).
Now collect exponents: for \(2\), \(-28 + 18 + 5 + 5 = 0\); for \(3\), \(7 - 6 = 1\); for \(5\), \(7 - 5 - 2 = 0\).
So the product is \(2^0\cdot 3^1\cdot 5^0 = 3\).
\(\therefore\) the left side \(= \log 3\).

Simplify each term. \(\sqrt{\log_2 x^4} = \sqrt{4\log_2 x} = 2\sqrt{\log_2 x}\).
\(4\log_4\sqrt{\frac{2}{x}} = 2\log_4\left(\frac{2}{x}\right) = 2\cdot\frac{\log_2\left(\frac{2}{x}\right)}{\log_2 4} = \log_2\left(\frac{2}{x}\right) = 1 - \log_2 x\).
Put \(t = \log_2 x\) (with \(t \ge 0\), needed for the square root). The equation becomes \(2\sqrt{t} + 1 - t = 2\), i.e. \(2\sqrt{t} = t + 1\).
Then \(t - 2\sqrt{t} + 1 = 0\), i.e. \(\left(\sqrt{t} - 1\right)^2 = 0\), so \(\sqrt{t} = 1\) and \(t = 1\).
Hence \(\log_2 x = 1\).
\(\therefore x = 2\).

Simplify the numerator: \(3 + \log_{10}343 = 3 + 3\log_{10}7 = 3\left(1 + \log_{10}7\right) = 3\log_{10}70\).
Simplify the denominator: \(\frac{1}{2}\log_{10}\left(\frac{49}{4}\right) = \log_{10}\frac{7}{2}\) and \(\frac{1}{2}\log_{10}\left(\frac{1}{25}\right) = \log_{10}\frac{1}{5}\),
so it is \(2 + \log_{10}\frac{7}{2} + \log_{10}\frac{1}{5} = 2 + \log_{10}\frac{7}{10} = \log_{10}100 + \log_{10}\frac{7}{10} = \log_{10}70\).
The quotient is \(\frac{3\log_{10}70}{\log_{10}70}\).
\(\therefore\) the value is \(3\).

Let each of the equal ratios be \(k\). Then
\(\log a = k(x+y-2z)\), \(\log b = k(y+z-2x)\), \(\log c = k(z+x-2y)\).
Add the three: the bracket total is \((x+y-2z)+(y+z-2x)+(z+x-2y) = 0\),
so \(\log a + \log b + \log c = k\cdot 0 = 0\).
Hence \(\log(abc) = 0\).
\(\therefore abc = 1\).

Bring the exponents down with \(\log_b m^n = n\log_b m\):
\(\log_y x^3\cdot\log_z y^4\cdot\log_x z^5 = 3\log_y x\cdot 4\log_z y\cdot 5\log_x z = 60\left(\log_y x\cdot\log_z y\cdot\log_x z\right)\).
Change all three to a common base: \(\log_y x\cdot\log_z y\cdot\log_x z = \frac{\log x}{\log y}\cdot\frac{\log y}{\log z}\cdot\frac{\log z}{\log x} = 1\).
\(\therefore \log_y x^3\cdot\log_z y^4\cdot\log_x z^5 = 60\times 1 = 60\).

Let each ratio be \(t\), so \(\log_2 a = 4t\), \(\log_2 b = 6t\), \(\log_2 c = 3kt\).
Take \(\log_2\) of \(a^3b^2c = 1\): \(3\log_2 a + 2\log_2 b + \log_2 c = \log_2 1 = 0\).
Substituting, \(3(4t) + 2(6t) + 3kt = 0\), i.e. \(t(24 + 3k) = 0\).
Since \(t \ne 0\) (otherwise \(a = b = c = 1\) and the given ratios are indeterminate), \(24 + 3k = 0\).
\(\therefore k = -8\).

Split the double inequality into two conditions.
\(|x-1| < 4\) gives \(-4 < x-1 < 4\), i.e. \(-3 < x < 5\).
\(|x-1| > 1\) gives \(x-1 > 1\) or \(x-1 < -1\), i.e. \(x > 2\) or \(x < 0\).
Intersecting \((-3,5)\) with \((-\infty,0)\cup(2,\infty)\):
\(\therefore x \in (-3, 0)\cup(2, 5)\).

Factorise: \(x^2 - x - 6 = (x-3)(x+2)\), so the equation is \(|x-3|\,|x+2| = x+2\).
A modulus is never negative, so we need \(x + 2 \ge 0\), i.e. \(x \ge -2\).
If \(x = -2\): left side \(= 0\) and right side \(= 0\), so \(x = -2\) is a solution.
If \(x > -2\): then \(|x+2| = x+2 > 0\), and dividing by it gives \(|x-3| = 1\), so \(x - 3 = \pm 1\), i.e. \(x = 4\) or \(x = 2\); both satisfy \(x > -2\).
Checking: \(x=2\) gives \(|-4| = 4 = 2+2\); \(x=4\) gives \(|6| = 6 = 4+2\).
\(\therefore x \in \{-2, 2, 4\}\).

Put \(t = x^2\), so \(t \ge 0\) and the equation is \(|t-9| + |t-4| = 5\).
If \(4 \le t \le 9\): \((9-t) + (t-4) = 5\), which is true for every such \(t\).
If \(t < 4\): \((9-t) + (4-t) = 13 - 2t > 5\), so no solution.
If \(t > 9\): \((t-9) + (t-4) = 2t - 13 > 5\), so no solution.
Hence \(4 \le x^2 \le 9\), i.e. \(2 \le |x| \le 3\).
\(\therefore x \in [-3, -2]\cup[2, 3]\).

\([x]\) is always an integer, so \(-2 < [x] \le 7\) means \([x]\) takes one of the values \(-1, 0, 1, \ldots, 7\).
For an integer \(n\), \([x] = n\) exactly when \(n \le x < n+1\).
So \(x\) lies in \([-1,0)\cup[0,1)\cup\cdots\cup[7,8)\), and these consecutive intervals join up.
\(\therefore x \in [-1, 8)\).
_note: Book answer-key error. The key prints (-2, 8); the correct solution set is [-1, 8), since [x] > -2 forces [x] >= -1 and hence x >= -1. x = -1.5 lies in the printed key but has [x] = -2, which fails -2 < [x].
The printed key lists this answer, [9/2, 5), against label f) rather than e). Our derived answer agrees with that value; only the key's labelling is off.

solution:
Let \([x] = n\), an integer, so \(n \le x < n+1\). The equation gives \([x^2] = 5n - 6\), which means \(5n - 6 \le x^2 < 5n - 5\).
If \(n \le 1\), the band requires \(x^2 < 5n-5 \le 0\), which is impossible since \(x^2 \ge 0\).
If \(n \ge 4\), then \(x \ge n\) forces \(x^2 \ge n^2\), and \(n^2 - (5n-5) = n^2-5n+5 > 0\) for \(n \ge 4\), so \(x^2\) is already past the band and no \(x\) works.
\(n = 2\): need \(2 \le x < 3\) and \(4 \le x^2 < 5\), giving \(2 \le x < \sqrt{5}\).
\(n = 3\): need \(3 \le x < 4\) and \(9 \le x^2 < 10\), giving \(3 \le x < \sqrt{10}\).
Checking \(x = 2.1\): \([4.41] - 5(2) + 6 = 4 - 10 + 6 = 0\); and \(x = 2.5\) fails since \([6.25] - 10 + 6 = 2\).
\(\therefore x \in \left[2, \sqrt{5}\right)\cup\left[3, \sqrt{10}\right)\).
_note: No usable printed key. The key's e) entry, [13/5, 7), matches no reading of this stem (nor of any other item of Q39); the key's f) entry, [9/2, 5), is in fact the answer to item e). Our answer [2, sqrt 5) u [3, sqrt 10) was derived unaided and verified by direct substitution.

solution:
Since \(2\) and \(-2\) are integers, \([x-2] = [x] - 2\) and \([x+2] = [x] + 2\).
So the equation becomes \(\left([x]-2\right) + \left([x]+2\right) + \{x\} = 0\), i.e. \(2[x] + \{x\} = 0\).
Let \([x] = n\) (an integer) and \(\{x\} = f\), where \(0 \le f < 1\). Then \(f = -2n\).
The condition \(0 \le -2n < 1\) gives \(-\frac{1}{2} < n \le 0\), and the only integer there is \(n = 0\); then \(f = 0\).
So \(x = n + f = 0\). Check: \([-2] + [2] + \{0\} = -2 + 2 + 0 = 0\).
\(\therefore x = 0\).

solution:
The left side is a sum of two integers, so \(\frac{5x}{6}\) must be an integer.
Also \([y] \le y\) for every real \(y\), with equality only when \(y\) is an integer. Hence
\(\left[\frac{x}{2}\right] + \left[\frac{x}{3}\right] \le \frac{x}{2} + \frac{x}{3} = \frac{5x}{6}\),
and the given equality holds only when \(\frac{x}{2}\) and \(\frac{x}{3}\) are both integers.
\(\frac{x}{2} \in \mathbb{Z}\) and \(\frac{x}{3} \in \mathbb{Z}\) together mean \(x\) is a multiple of \(6\).
Check \(x = 6\): \([3] + [2] = 5 = \frac{5(6)}{6}\); and \(x = -6\): \([-3] + [-2] = -5 = \frac{5(-6)}{6}\).
\(\therefore x = 6k\), where \(k \in \mathbb{Z}\) (all integer multiples of \(6\)).

solution:
\(f\) is a ratio of polynomials, so the only restriction is that the denominator must not vanish.
\(x^2 + x - 6 = (x+3)(x-2)\), which is \(0\) when \(x = -3\) or \(x = 2\).
\(\therefore\) domain \(= \mathbb{R} - \{-3,\ 2\}\).

solution:
Three conditions must hold together.
The square root needs \(x - 3 \ge 0\), i.e. \(x \ge 3\).
The logarithm needs \(5 - x > 0\), i.e. \(x < 5\).
The logarithm is in a denominator, so \(\log(5-x) \ne 0\), i.e. \(5 - x \ne 1\), i.e. \(x \ne 4\).
Combining: \(3 \le x < 5\) with \(x \ne 4\).
\(\therefore\) domain \(= [3, 4)\cup(4, 5)\).

Work from the innermost root outwards.
Innermost: \(1 - x^2 \ge 0\), i.e. \(x^2 \le 1\), i.e. \(-1 \le x \le 1\).
For such \(x\), \(\sqrt{1-x^2} \in [0,1]\), so \(1 - \sqrt{1-x^2} \in [0,1]\), which is already \(\ge 0\).
Then \(\sqrt{1-\sqrt{1-x^2}} \in [0,1]\), so \(1 - \sqrt{1-\sqrt{1-x^2}} \in [0,1] \ge 0\).
So the outer two roots impose no extra restriction.
\(\therefore\) domain \(= [-1, 1]\).

\(x!\) is defined by \(x! = x(x-1)(x-2)\cdots 2\cdot 1\) with \(0! = 1\), so it has a meaning only when \(x\) is a non-negative integer (there is no factorial of a negative number or of a fraction such as \(\frac{3}{2}\)).
\(\therefore\) domain \(= \{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots\}\), the set of whole numbers (\(\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}\)).

For \({}^{n}P_{r}\) to be defined we need \(n\) and \(r\) to be integers with \(0 \le r \le n\). Here \(n = 5-x\) and \(r = x-1\).
So \(x\) must be an integer, and:
\(r \ge 0\) gives \(x - 1 \ge 0\), i.e. \(x \ge 1\);
\(r \le n\) gives \(x - 1 \le 5 - x\), i.e. \(2x \le 6\), i.e. \(x \le 3\).
So \(x\) is an integer with \(1 \le x \le 3\). Checking: \(x=1\) gives \({}^{4}P_{0}\), \(x=2\) gives \({}^{3}P_{1}\), \(x=3\) gives \({}^{2}P_{2}\), all defined.
\(\therefore\) domain \(= \{1, 2, 3\}\).

Both square roots need non-negative radicands.
\(x - x^2 \ge 0\) gives \(x(1-x) \ge 0\), i.e. \(0 \le x \le 1\).
\(5 - x \ge 0\) gives \(x \le 5\).
The intersection of \([0,1]\) and \((-\infty, 5]\) is \([0,1]\).
\(\therefore\) domain \(= [0, 1]\).

The square root needs \(\log(x^2-6x+6) \ge 0\), i.e. \(x^2 - 6x + 6 \ge 10^0 = 1\).
So \(x^2 - 6x + 5 \ge 0\), i.e. \((x-1)(x-5) \ge 0\), giving \(x \le 1\) or \(x \ge 5\).
(This automatically makes \(x^2-6x+6 \ge 1 > 0\), so the logarithm itself is defined.)
\(\therefore\) domain \(= (-\infty, 1]\cup[5, \infty)\).

A modulus is never negative, so \(|x-5| \ge 0\) for every real \(x\).
The value \(0\) is attained at \(x = 5\), and \(|x-5|\) grows without bound as \(x\) moves away from \(5\), taking every positive value.
\(\therefore\) range \(= [0, \infty)\).

solution:
Let \(y = \frac{x}{9+x^2}\). Then \(y(9+x^2) = x\), i.e. \(yx^2 - x + 9y = 0\).
If \(y = 0\), this gives \(x = 0\), so \(y = 0\) is attained.
If \(y \ne 0\), it is a quadratic in \(x\), and \(x\) is real only if its discriminant is non-negative:
\((-1)^2 - 4(y)(9y) \ge 0\), i.e. \(1 - 36y^2 \ge 0\), i.e. \(y^2 \le \frac{1}{36}\), i.e. \(-\frac{1}{6} \le y \le \frac{1}{6}\).
The end values are attained: \(x = 3\) gives \(y = \frac{1}{6}\) and \(x = -3\) gives \(y = -\frac{1}{6}\).
\(\therefore\) range \(= \left[-\frac{1}{6},\ \frac{1}{6}\right]\).

The domain is \(x \ge 0\), so \(\sqrt{x}\) takes every value in \([0, \infty)\).
Then \(1 + \sqrt{x}\) takes every value in \([1, \infty)\), and taking reciprocals reverses the order.
So \(f(x) = \frac{1}{1+\sqrt{x}}\) takes every value in \((0, 1]\): the value \(1\) at \(x = 0\), and values approaching \(0\) (never equal to \(0\)) as \(x \to \infty\).
\(\therefore\) range \(= (0, 1]\).

By definition of the fractional part, \(\{x\} = x - [x]\), so \(f(x) = [x] - x = -\{x\}\).
Now \(0 \le \{x\} < 1\) for every real \(x\), and \(\{x\}\) attains every value in \([0,1)\).
Multiplying by \(-1\) reverses the inequalities: \(-1 < -\{x\} \le 0\).
\(\therefore\) range \(= (-1, 0]\).

Put \(t = 2^x\); as \(x\) runs over \(\mathbb{R}\), \(t\) takes every value in \((0, \infty)\). Since \(4^x = \left(2^x\right)^2 = t^2\),
\(f = 1 + t + t^2\).
On \(t > 0\) this is strictly increasing, so it takes every value between its limits: as \(t \to 0^{+}\), \(f \to 1\) (not attained), and as \(t \to \infty\), \(f \to \infty\).
\(\therefore\) range \(= (1, \infty)\).

\((f\circ g)(x) = f\left(g(x)\right) = f(\log x) = e^{\log x} = x\), defined for \(x > 0\).
\((g\circ f)(x) = g\left(f(x)\right) = g(e^x) = \log\left(e^x\right) = x\), defined for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\).
\(\therefore (f\circ g)(x) = x\) (for \(x>0\)) and \((g\circ f)(x) = x\) (for \(x \in \mathbb{R}\)); \(f\) and \(g\) are inverses of each other.

\((g\circ f)(x) = g\left(f(x)\right) = \left[f(x)\right]^2 + f(x) - 2\), and this equals \(4x^2 - 10x + 4\).
So \(\left[f(x)\right]^2 + f(x) = 4x^2 - 10x + 6\). Complete the square on the left by adding \(\frac{1}{4}\):
\(\left[f(x) + \frac{1}{2}\right]^2 = 4x^2 - 10x + \frac{25}{4} = \left(2x - \frac{5}{2}\right)^2\).
Hence \(f(x) + \frac{1}{2} = \pm\left(2x - \frac{5}{2}\right)\), giving \(f(x) = 2x - 3\) or \(f(x) = 2 - 2x\).
Check \(f(x) = 2x-3\): \(g(2x-3) = (2x-3)^2 + (2x-3) - 2 = 4x^2 - 10x + 4\).
\(\therefore f(x) = 2x - 3\) (the linear function \(f(x) = 2 - 2x\) also satisfies the condition).

solution:
Put \(t = g(x) = 1 + \sqrt{x}\), so that \(\sqrt{x} = t - 1\) and \(x = (t-1)^2\).
Then \(f\left[g(x)\right] = f(t)\), and rewriting the right side in terms of \(t\):
\(3 + 2\sqrt{x} + x = 3 + 2(t-1) + (t-1)^2 = 3 + 2t - 2 + t^2 - 2t + 1 = t^2 + 2\).
So \(f(t) = t^2 + 2\) for every \(t\) in the range of \(g\).
Check: \(f\left(1+\sqrt{x}\right) = \left(1+\sqrt{x}\right)^2 + 2 = 1 + 2\sqrt{x} + x + 2 = 3 + 2\sqrt{x} + x\).
\(\therefore f(x) = x^2 + 2\).

\((f\circ f)(x) = f\left(f(x)\right) = \dfrac{f(x)}{\sqrt{1 + \left[f(x)\right]^2}}\), where \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\).
First, \(1 + \left[f(x)\right]^2 = 1 + \frac{x^2}{1+x^2} = \frac{1+x^2+x^2}{1+x^2} = \frac{1+2x^2}{1+x^2}\).
So \((f\circ f)(x) = \dfrac{\frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}}{\sqrt{\frac{1+2x^2}{1+x^2}}} = \frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\times\frac{\sqrt{1+x^2}}{\sqrt{1+2x^2}}\).
\(\therefore (f\circ f)(x) = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+2x^2}}\), for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\).

solution:
\((f\circ f)(x) = f\left(f(x)\right) = \dfrac{2f(x) + 1}{3f(x) - 2}\), where \(f(x) = \dfrac{2x+1}{3x-2}\).
Numerator: \(2\left(\frac{2x+1}{3x-2}\right) + 1 = \frac{4x+2+3x-2}{3x-2} = \frac{7x}{3x-2}\).
Denominator: \(3\left(\frac{2x+1}{3x-2}\right) - 2 = \frac{6x+3-6x+4}{3x-2} = \frac{7}{3x-2}\).
Dividing, \((f\circ f)(x) = \frac{7x}{3x-2}\times\frac{3x-2}{7} = x\).
\(\therefore (f\circ f)(x) = x\), for \(x \ne \frac{2}{3}\) (so \(f\) is its own inverse).
